title: Nebensatz — Subordinate clauses in German
schema: english-prompt -> learner types German -> Reveal answer shows reference + mic

exercises.english: Because he is tired, he goes to bed early.
exercises.german: Weil er müde ist, geht er früh ins Bett.
exercises.why: A weil-clause is subordinate: the conjugated verb goes last, then the main clause follows.

exercises.english: I hope that you will come soon.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass du bald kommst.
exercises.why: dass-clause: verb last, matching the subject du.

exercises.english: If the weather stays nice, we are having a picnic.
exercises.german: Wenn das Wetter schön bleibt, machen wir ein Picknick.
exercises.why: Subordinate clause: verb last, and bleibt agrees with the singular subject das Wetter.

exercises.english: Although it is raining, we are going by bike.
exercises.german: Obwohl es regnet, fahren wir mit dem Rad.
exercises.why: obwohl-clause is subordinate: fahren last, without the pronoun wir.

exercises.english: After we have eaten, we are going for a walk.
exercises.german: Nachdem wir gegessen haben, gehen wir spazieren.
exercises.why: With haben the participle forms the Perfekt: gegessen haben.

exercises.english: Before I go to work, I drink a coffee.
exercises.german: Bevor ich zur Arbeit gehe, trinke ich einen Kaffee.
exercises.why: gehen takes gehe in the first person - the e to i change.

exercises.english: The man who lives next to me is very kind.
exercises.german: Der Mann, der neben mir wohnt, ist sehr freundlich.
exercises.why: Relative clause on der: verb last, singular subject, and a Präteritum would need a time reference.

exercises.english: The woman whose son studies in Switzerland is my neighbour.
exercises.german: Die Frau, deren Sohn in der Schweiz studiert, ist meine Nachbarin.
exercises.why: Relative clause on deren: verb last, and studieren would not agree with the singular subject ihr Sohn.

exercises.english: It is important that you come on time.
exercises.german: Es ist wichtig, dass du pünktlich kommst.
exercises.why: es ist wichtig, dass … keeps the verb in final position.

exercises.english: I have a question about whether we can start earlier.
exercises.german: Ich habe eine Frage, ob wir früher anfangen können.
exercises.why: Infinitival clause: the modal können stands last, anfangen stays at the start.

exercises.english: When she gets nervous, everything goes wrong for her.
exercises.german: Sie hat Angst, dass es schiefgeht.
exercises.why: Separable verb: the prefix schief- rejoins the verb, so the whole verb geht is the last word of the dass-clause.

exercises.english: Assuming we had more time, we would travel to Japan.
exercises.german: Angenommen, wir hätten mehr Zeit, würden wir nach Japan reisen.
exercises.why: Irreal condition: hätten in the clause, würde + Position II + infinitive last in the main clause.

exercises.english: As long as you are healthy, you should get plenty of exercise.
exercises.german: Solange man gesund ist, sollte man sich viel bewegen.
exercises.why: solange-clause: verb last; man takes the singular form ist.

exercises.english: As soon as the film starts, the phone has to go.
exercises.german: Sobald der Film anfängt, muss das Handy weg.
exercises.why: Modal in Position II of the main clause, singular because das Handy is singular.

exercises.english: He called me so that I can help him.
exercises.german: Er rief mich an, damit ich ihm helfe.
exercises.why: damit-clause: verb last; helfen with the dative gives helfe.

exercises.english: The flat we have rented is on the third floor.
exercises.german: Die Wohnung, die wir gemietet haben, liegt im dritten Stock.
exercises.why: Relative clause: the auxiliary haben goes last after the participle.

exercises.english: I still do not know whether I have time.
exercises.german: Ob ich Zeit habe, weiß ich noch nicht.
exercises.why: ob-indirect question: verb last. was ich habe carries the negation, not the answer.

exercises.english: I am glad that you are coming today.
exercises.german: Es freut mich, dass du heute kommst.
exercises.why: dass-clause: verb last, matching du.

exercises.english: I believe that he is coming.
exercises.german: Ich glaube, dass er kommt.
exercises.why: Every subordinate clause takes a comma before the conjunction and after the clause.

exercises.english: If you have time, please come along.
exercises.german: Wenn du Zeit hast, komm bitte mit.
exercises.why: One comma opens the clause; no second comma follows it.

exercises.english: He said that he was ill.
exercises.german: Er sagte, dass er krank sei.
exercises.why: Reported speech uses Konjunktiv II and is written with dass.

exercises.english: Although it is raining, we are going.
exercises.german: Obwohl es regnet, gehen wir.
exercises.why: The comma closes the clause; no comma before a short infinitive phrase.

exercises.english: I know that he is coming, but I told you so.
exercises.german: Ich weiß, dass er kommt, aber ich habe es dir gesagt.
exercises.why: Two main clauses joined by aber each take their own comma.

exercises.english: After he had eaten, he went for a walk.
exercises.german: Nachdem er gegessen hat, ging er spazieren.
exercises.why: The Perfekt belongs inside the clause: gegessen hat, then the comma.

exercises.english: The flat that we rent is rather expensive.
exercises.german: Die Wohnung, die wir mieten, ist ziemlich teuer.
exercises.why: das is the relative pronoun for neuter objects; the verb mieten goes last inside the clause.

exercises.english: It doesn't matter to me whether it rains.
exercises.german: Es ist mir egal, ob es regnet.
exercises.why: Comma before ob and after the end of the clause.

exercises.english: Before you go, please close the window.
exercises.german: Bevor du gehst, mach bitte das Fenster zu.
exercises.why: The comma closes the clause; no comma before the short infinitive.

exercises.english: I hope that it works out.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass es klappt.
exercises.why: Comma before dass and after the clause.

exercises.english: I'm coming later because I still have to work.
exercises.german: Ich komme später, weil ich noch arbeiten muss.
exercises.why: A trailing subordinate clause takes its own comma; it cannot lead a clause that repeats its subject.

exercises.english: Because I was tired, I went to bed early.
exercises.german: Weil ich müde war, ging ich früh ins Bett.
exercises.why: Fronted subordinate clause is set off by a comma; the main clause keeps normal word order.

exercises.english: I forgot that I had to cancel the appointment.
exercises.german: Ich habe vergessen, dass ich den Termin absagen musste.
exercises.why: Main clause verb in position II, then the dass-clause with its verb last.

exercises.english: I'm sorry that I'm coming so late.
exercises.german: Es tut mir leid, dass ich so spät komme.
exercises.why: tut + dative + es, then a dass-clause in final position.

exercises.english: I believe that he is coming tomorrow.
exercises.german: Ich glaube, dass er morgen kommt.
exercises.why: Inside the clause the subject er comes before the verb kommt.

exercises.english: We are glad that the exam went well.
exercises.german: Wir sind froh, dass die Prüfung gut ausgegangen ist.
exercises.why: The Perfekt needs both parts: ausgegangen ist, with ist last.

exercises.english: The colleague with whom I'm running the project is on holiday.
exercises.german: Der Kollege, mit dem ich das Projekt leite, ist im Urlaub.
exercises.why: In a prepositional relative clause the whole verb cluster sits at the end.

exercises.english: I asked him whether he would help me.
exercises.german: Ich habe ihn gefragt, ob er mir helfen würde.
exercises.why: The würde + infinitive cluster goes last inside the ob-clause.

exercises.english: Before we start, we still have to buy the material.
exercises.german: Bevor wir anfangen, müssen wir noch das Material kaufen.
exercises.why: bevor-clause with verb last, comma, then the main clause in position II.

exercises.english: She says that she is coming.
exercises.german: Sie sagt, dass sie kommt.
exercises.why: Subject sie then verb kommt, both inside the dass-clause.

exercises.english: Because he was ill, he stayed at home.
exercises.german: Weil er krank war, blieb er zu Hause.
exercises.why: weil starts a subordinate clause, so its verb war goes last. denn would need main-clause word order and no comma.

exercises.english: I'm not coming because I don't have time.
exercises.german: Ich komme nicht, denn ich habe keine Zeit.
exercises.why: denn keeps the main clause order: zweite conjugierte Verb habe stays in position II.

exercises.english: It's important that people arrive on time.
exercises.german: Es ist wichtig, dass man pünktlich kommt.
exercises.why: dass introduces a statement; wenn would introduce a condition, ob a question.

exercises.english: I doubt whether he is telling the truth.
exercises.german: Ich bezweifle, dass er die Wahrheit sagt.
exercises.why: A dass-clause reports a doubt: the verb bezweifle stays in Position II, and sagt is last inside the clause.

exercises.english: Do you know whether the train is arriving on time?
exercises.german: Weißt du, ob der Zug pünktlich kommt?
exercises.why: ob asks whether something is the case and puts the verb last.

exercises.english: He stays at home because he has caught a cold.
exercises.german: Er bleibt zu Hause, weil er sich erkältet hat.
exercises.why: weil states a cause; obwohl would contradict what the sentence asserts.

exercises.english: When I moved to Berlin in 1990, I was twenty.
exercises.german: Als ich 1990 nach Berlin zog, war ich zwanzig.
exercises.why: als narrates one completed event in the past; wenn is used for repeated or uncertain events.

exercises.english: When I was a child, I was allowed to play for a long time.
exercises.german: Wenn ich ein Kind war, durfte ich lange spielen.
exercises.why: winden covers a repeated situation; als is reserved for a single completed event.

exercises.english: Since I have lived here, I have got to know a lot of people.
exercises.german: Seit ich hier wohne, kenne ich viele Leute.
exercises.why: seit with the present tense marks a situation that started in the past and still holds.

exercises.english: Wait here until I come back.
exercises.german: Warte hier, bis ich zurückkomme.
exercises.why: bis marks the end point of a waiting period.

exercises.english: After I had eaten, I went for a walk.
exercises.german: Nachdem ich gegessen hatte, ging ich spazieren.
exercises.why: nachdem places one completed past action before another.

exercises.english: I'll explain it one more time so that everyone understands.
exercises.german: Ich erkläre es noch einmal, damit alle es verstehen.
exercises.why: damit forms its own clause with a subject; um … zu has no subject of its own.

exercises.english: I save time so that I can get home earlier.
exercises.german: Ich spare Zeit, um früher nach Hause zu kommen.
exercises.why: um … zu replaces damit when main and subordinate subject are identical.

exercises.english: It was so cold that we all stayed at home.
exercises.german: Es war so kalt, dass wir alle zu Hause blieben.
exercises.why: so … dass states a consequence; damit would state a purpose.

exercises.english: The roads were slippery, so we had to drive slowly.
exercises.german: Die Straßen waren glatt, sodass wir langsam fahren mussten.
exercises.why: The result clause may be written sodass as one word; inside it the verb still comes last.

exercises.english: While I am cooking, my brother is making a phone call.
exercises.german: Während ich koche, telefoniert mein Bruder.
exercises.why: während with the present tense covers two simultaneous actions.

exercises.english: Before we set off, we have to switch off the light.
exercises.german: Bevor wir losgehen, müssen wir das Licht ausschalten.
exercises.why: bevor puts one action ahead of the other; the main clause states what follows.

exercises.english: If it happens to rain, we will take a taxi.
exercises.german: Falls es regnet, nehmen wir ein Taxi.
exercises.why: falls introduces a possible condition and takes the verb last.

exercises.english: He spoke slowly, so that everyone understood him.
exercises.german: Er sprach langsam, sodass alle ihn verstanden.
exercises.why: sodass states a consequence that follows from speaking slowly.

exercises.english: He said that he is coming.
exercises.german: Er sagte, dass er kommt.
exercises.why: sagen plus dass forms a subordinate clause, so kommt comes last.

exercises.english: Although he was tired, he went on working.
exercises.german: Obwohl er müde war, arbeitete er weiter.
exercises.why: obwohl-clause with verb last; the main clause keeps normal order.

exercises.english: It is necessary that you fill in the form.
exercises.german: Es ist notwendig, dass man das Formular ausfüllt.
exercises.why: A dass-clause needs its own finite verb (ausfüllt). An infinitive alone cannot be the clause verb.

exercises.english: He says that he has already seen the film.
exercises.german: Er sagt, dass er den Film schon gesehen hat.
exercises.why: Inside the clause the Perfekt is gesehen hat, with the auxiliary in final position.

exercises.english: If I had more time, I would take a course.
exercises.german: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, würde ich einen Kurs besuchen.
exercises.why: Irreal condition: hätte in the wenn-clause, würde + infinitive in the main clause.

exercises.english: If I had had more time, I would have taken a course.
exercises.german: Wenn ich mehr Zeit gehabt hätte, würde ich einen Kurs besucht haben.
exercises.why: Plusquamperfekt in the clause and würde + Perfekt in the main clause.

exercises.english: I hope that the form will be handed in on time.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass das Formular rechtzeitig abgegeben wird.
exercises.why: The whole modal-passive cluster is only abgegeben wird here; the auxiliary wird is the last word of the clause.

exercises.english: I hope that the bill will be paid soon.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass die Rechnung bald bezahlt wird.
exercises.why: The whole werden-passive cluster sits last inside the clause.

exercises.english: I had to work because the train was delayed.
exercises.german: Ich habe arbeiten müssen, weil der Zug Verspätung hatte.
exercises.why: Modal Perfekt keeps the infinitive before the auxiliary: arbeiten müssen. A comma also closes the weil-clause.

exercises.english: I hope that the delivery will arrive tomorrow.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass die Lieferung morgen ankommt.
exercises.why: In the subordinate clause the separable prefix rejoins the verb: ankommt.

exercises.english: It is important that you take notes and read the sources.
exercises.german: Es ist wichtig, dass du abschreibst und die Quellen liest.
exercises.why: In coordinated clauses sharing one subject, only the first verb goes final.

exercises.english: I do not know whether I will be able to take part.
exercises.german: Ich weiß nicht, ob ich teilnehmen kann.
exercises.why: In an ob-clause the modal kann stands last, with the infinitive in front of it.

exercises.english: He is gone because the door was closed.
exercises.german: Er ist weg, weil die Tür geschlossen wurde.
exercises.why: Passive of werden in the Präteritum: wurde geschlossen, auxiliary last.

exercises.english: I hope that I can pay the bill on time.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass ich die Rechnung pünktlich bezahlen kann.
exercises.why: Modal kann is the finite verb of the dass-clause and goes last, with the infinitive bezahlen in front of it.

exercises.english: I hope that I will pass the course.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass ich den Kurs bestehen werde.
exercises.why: werden as a finite verb goes last; the infinitive stays in front of it.

exercises.english: The man standing over there is my boss.
exercises.german: Der Mann, der dort steht, ist mein Chef.
exercises.why: der is the relative pronoun for masculine persons; the verb steht goes last.

exercises.english: The book that I bought is expensive.
exercises.german: Das Buch, das ich gekauft habe, ist teuer.
exercises.why: The relative pronoun takes the case of its role inside the clause: das as the object of gekauft habe.

exercises.english: That is the neighbour whose child is at school.
exercises.german: Das ist die Nachbarin, deren Kind in der Schule ist.
exercises.why: deren replaces des + possessive and agrees with the following noun.

exercises.english: The dog whose owner is ill stays home alone.
exercises.german: Der Hund, dessen Besitzer krank ist, bleibt allein.
exercises.why: dessen replaces des + possessive; the clause keeps its own verb order, so ist stays last.

exercises.english: That is the café where we met each other.
exercises.german: Das ist das Café, wo wir uns kennengelernt haben.
exercises.why: wo replaces in + location and stands without a preposition; wohin would mean direction.

exercises.english: That is the street we walked to.
exercises.german: Das ist die Straße, wohin wir gegangen sind.
exercises.why: wohin replaces in + accusative for movement; wo would imply a fixed location.

exercises.english: I still remember the day when we moved house.
exercises.german: Ich erinnere mich an den Tag, wann wir umgezogen sind.
exercises.why: wann replaces an einem + time and stands without a preposition.

exercises.english: I know what I should say.
exercises.german: Ich weiß, was ich sagen soll.
exercises.why: was stands for things and for the content of a whole clause.

exercises.english: Whoever does not know that has to guess.
exercises.german: Wer das nicht weiß, muss raten.
exercises.why: wer stands for an unnamed person and takes over the subject of the main clause.

exercises.english: That is the film we talked about.
exercises.german: Das ist der Film, über den wir gesprochen haben.
exercises.why: A preposition stands before the relative pronoun: über den, with den as the accusative object.

exercises.english: I know someone I get along with really well.
exercises.german: Ich kenne jemanden, mit dem ich gut auskommen bin.
exercises.why: mit dem: the preposition stands first, dem is the dative object of auskommen.

exercises.english: I know a colleague I work closely with.
exercises.german: Ich kenne eine Kollegin, mit der ich viel zusammenarbeite.
exercises.why: For a feminine person the relative pronoun is welche; with a preposition it becomes mit der.

exercises.english: It is possible that we will start earlier.
exercises.german: Es ist möglich, dass wir früher anfangen.
exercises.why: A modal main clause plus a dass-clause: anfangen goes last inside the clause.

exercises.english: I hope that I can take part.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass ich teilnehmen kann.
exercises.why: Inside an ob-clause the modal kann is the finite verb and goes last.

exercises.english: Because it was raining and the streets were slippery, we stayed at home.
exercises.german: Weil es regnete und die Straßen glatt waren, sind wir zu Hause geblieben.
exercises.why: The first subordinate clause is verb-final; the second shares its subject and keeps Position III.

exercises.english: If you feel like it, you are very welcome to come along.
exercises.german: Wenn du willst, kannst du gerne mitkommen.
exercises.why: wenn-clause with willst last, then kannst in Position II of the main clause.

exercises.english: I think he is coming, because he promised to.
exercises.german: Ich glaube, dass er kommt, weil er es versprochen hat.
exercises.why: Both clauses are verb-final and each is closed by its own comma.

exercises.english: I hope that the colleague who is helping me has time.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass der Kollege, der mir hilft, Zeit hat.
exercises.why: The relative clause sits inside the dass-clause and keeps its own verb-last order.

exercises.english: I do not have time to talk with you.
exercises.german: Ich habe keine Zeit, um mit dir zu sprechen.
exercises.why: um … zu keeps its infinitive at the end: mit dir zu sprechen.

exercises.english: It is important that you submit the results on time.
exercises.german: Es ist wichtig, dass du die Ergebnisse rechtzeitig vorlegst.
exercises.why: A dass-clause after es ist wichtig needs its own finite verb: vorlegst sits at the end.

exercises.english: While you are cooking, I can already set the table.
exercises.german: Während du kochst, kann ich schon den Tisch decken.
exercises.why: während-clause with verb last, then kann in Position II of the main clause.

exercises.english: He said that he is coming later, because he is stuck in traffic.
exercises.german: Er sagte, dass er später kommt, weil er im Stau steht.
exercises.why: dass-clause and weil-clause are both verb-final, each closed by a comma.

exercises.english: As soon as I have read the text, I will call you.
exercises.german: Sobald ich den Text gelesen habe, rufe ich dich an.
exercises.why: sobold-clause with the Perfekt: gelesen habe, with habe last.

exercises.english: I am glad that you are coming.
exercises.german: Ich freue mich, dass du kommst.
exercises.why: sich freuen auf/dass takes a dass-clause with verb-final order.

exercises.english: If it rains, I know that we are staying at home.
exercises.german: Wenn es regnet, weiß ich, dass wir zu Hause bleiben.
exercises.why: The wenn-clause ends the sentence, so no comma; the internal dass-clause is verb-final.

exercises.english: I am looking for someone who knows whether the position is still available.
exercises.german: Ich suche jemanden, der weiß, ob die Stelle noch frei ist.
exercises.why: Nested clauses: the relative clause is verb-final, and the ob-clause inside it is too.

exercises.english: I am sorry that the application was not approved.
exercises.german: Es tut mir leid, dass der Antrag nicht genehmigt wurde.
exercises.why: Passive with wurde: the auxiliary steht last inside the dass-clause.

exercises.english: If I were you, I would take the job.
exercises.german: Wenn ich du wärst, würde ich die Stelle annehmen.
exercises.why: Irreal comparison: wärst in the wenn-clause, würde + infinitive in the main clause.
